utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to one and all. Madam Registrar, would you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-96-23/2-PT, The Prosecutor versus Radovan Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam. May we have the appearances for the parties. The Prosecution first, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Jan Wubben for the Prosecution team, together with my co-counsel Ms. Patricia Sellers and Manoj Sachdeva. And the case manager, Djurdja Mirkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. And for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am Milenko Radovic, lawyer, and the Defence counsel for the accused, Mr. Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Stankovic, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you in the Serbian language. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I should like to remind the parties that we are here today for a Status Conference pursuant to Rule 65 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. I think that the Prosecution has agreed to the demand for an amended indictment. I don't want to go into details. But I think that we're now at a stage where we have a final -- actually, we're in the final stage. And my question to the Prosecution would be as follows: Does the Prosecution envisage filing its pre-trial brief, and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for starting this issue. Yes, as a subsequent phase, we would like to draft our pre-trial brief. And we can file it within a couple of weeks if you requested us to do so. So we might even anticipate filing our pre-trial brief by the latest at the end of this month.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the 31st of March? You will be ready by the 31st of March. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Since we're here, I should like to receive assurances that the Prosecution has fulfilled its tasks pursuant to Rule 66, 67, and perhaps even 68 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I can confirm, Your Honour, we are on a basis of continuing communications with Defence counsel with that view. We give Defence counsel an overview of our disclosures, and we also check with counsel on a regular basis whenever he has additional needs for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And perhaps a final remark with respect to the Prosecution: Have you received a follow-up to the letter sent out by the Defence raising the possibility of presenting a defence by alibi?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we didn't receive any explicit follow-up on that letter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I am now going to turn to the Defence. Could you please confirm whether what the Prosecution said is correct, and has the Prosecution fulfilled its tasks pursuant to the articles I mentioned? That is to say, Rule 66, 67, and 68 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as my learned colleague has just said, Mr. Wubben, in between the two Status Conferences and in keeping with the agreement we both are signatories to, we exchanged documents, and there were no problems on that score. The exchange of documents was conducted pursuant to Rules 66 and 67 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. The Defence intends at the earliest possible opportunity to supply the Prosecution with some more evidence that was collected by our investigators and which we will certainly be using as evidence in the Defence case. With respect to a Defence of alibi, you asked me to say a few words about that as well, the Defence is processing that evidence, too, and it will be informing the Prosecution in due course pursuant to Rule 67(i)(A). For its motion, the Defence was ready pursuant to your ruling of October. So we are ready to file that motion once the Prosecution does the same. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but just so that we agree, if the Prosecution is proposing to file its motion on the 31st of March, file its brief by the 31st of March, do you need two months, three months in order to file your pre-trial brief as a response to the Prosecution's?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this point in time, I can say for certain. I think that we should need at least two months. But once I see the brief filed by the Prosecution and can read through the facts, then I shall be able to tell you exactly. But I think two months is the minimum time that I should require. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I learned now, and that's new to me, not the alibi evidence as a possibility, but new to me is that there is an announcement that the Defence counsel will process evidence in that regard. When I informed you that we are ready to file by the end of the month, then it's also, without any question, of importance for us to include in our pre-trial brief our position that we take with a view to that alibi evidence. So I would like to request through you to the Defence counsel whether it's possible to process this evidence in time so that we are able to anticipate in our pre-trial brief with a view to that defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you for those remarks. But as far as I was able to understand as to what the Defence said, at this point in time, we are not ready to pronounce ourselves in the matter. It will require research. So, therefore, I think that we will not have to declare ourselves at this point in time, at this stage. What I'm suggesting is that you can present your pre-trial brief by the date we mentioned, that is to say, the 31st of March, and then the Defence has asked for at least two months - I think they said that was the minimum time they would need - and then the possibility is open to the Defence of presenting a defence of alibi. But the Defence cannot be obliged to state its views at this point in time, but I do understand your concerns. In as far as filing your pre-trial brief, you would, of course, like to be able to respond to the Defence arguments in that respect. But I think that the Defence is quite clear, and I should like to have confirmation from the Defence that I followed his argumentation properly, which was that the Defence can't state its views definitively at this point in time. So I propose that you file the pre-trial brief by the date we mentioned, that is to say, the 31st of March. And then the Defence will have, shall I say, at least two months. We can give them three months a priori from this date forward. And I think that the Defence will be able, then, to state clearly what its position is with respect to the defence of alibi, because if I have understood you correctly, and please tell me whether I have followed your arguments correctly, sir, that at this point in time you are engaged in research. But you are not ready to establish, to draw up a document here and now, or to state your position here and now with respect to that matter. And that you are, in fact, waiting to see how your research develops.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you have understood me completely. And the Defence at this point in time, as I said, is not ready. We are working with certain witnesses. We're looking into which witnesses we shall be calling and what evidence we shall be using in our defence of alibi. I shall try, I shall do my best, that in the pre-trial brief, we indicate the facts and circumstances that we're going to focus on and which witnesses the Defence will be calling for its defence of alibi. But at this point in time, we can't do that. It is an ongoing process that we're working on at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now my final question is this: Would three months be sufficient? Do you agree to a period of three months? Would that suffice to file your pre-trial brief within that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that will be sufficient. I think three months will suffice for our pre-trial brief, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So we have reached our first decision, and that is that the Prosecution will file its pre-trial brief on the 31st of March. And following that, after the 31st of March, that is to say from the 1st of April in actual fact, the Defence will be given a period of three months to do the same, which makes it the end of June. I should now like to address Mr. Stankovic, to ask him -- or rather to ask him a few questions. First of all, with respect to your health, what is your health situation? Would you like to raise this matter in open session, or would you like us to go into private session, closed or private session, whichever?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have already spoken about my health situation. The health situation is as you wish it to be. You have incarcerated me. And this state continues, so I cannot be good. My health cannot be good in view of that fact. But if you will allow me to continue with what I wanted to say here today, I have prepared a short address for this Status Conference. May I be allowed to proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, Mr. Stankovic. Let's take first things first and one by one. First of all, your state of health. You have nothing particular to note in that regard, to tell me with respect to your health situation. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now, this brings me to my second question. I'd like to take advantage of this opportunity to clear up some misunderstandings between you, it appears, and the Registrar. That is to say, the other side, the other party. And I think it is that matter that you wish to address. Before you do so, I should like to explain my point of view. What I have understood personally -- Madam Registrar, is there a problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Sorry. I apologise, Your Honour, for being so rude to interrupt for a moment. But as I notice from the correspondence in this affair, the decision-making and also the decision-making by ICTY and the request from the parties had made on a confidential basis. It's just that fact that I know that is from a confidential basis that I give you into consideration to take in this phase already a decision whether or not you proceed in closed session or a more or less confidential way. That's the reason. Sorry to...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it can't be closed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment. Nobody has the right to speak before I give them permission to do so officially. Now, I'm following what you have said. And I should like to proceed with prudence with respect to what you're trying to draw my attention to, that aspect of the matter. And I think that everybody here is very wary and vigilant and would like to see the procedure evolves in a proper form. If I see that matters are progressing in the manner in matters which would require a private session, then I shall do so. But I think that Mr. Stankovic, and you yourselves, as indeed I do, I am, we are all fully conscious of the importance and sensitivity of the issue. And it's a good thing that you drew my attention to that. And I should like, Mr. Stankovic, in his response to bear in mind the character, the sensitive character, of the subject matter we're going to discuss. We know what it's all about. We're not going to enter into details because I have no intention of going into the details. Rest assured about that. I should just like to give you my personal impressions. And that is -- those are that Mr. Stankovic did not have the intention when he spoke his thoughts, if I can put it that way, they were spontaneous thoughts that were uttered. He didn't have the intention of violating the protective measures we put in place for certain subjects. So I should like to receive assurances on that point. Have I understood that correctly? I had the impression that Mr. Stankovic was convinced, or rather I had the opportunity of reading exchanges and correspondence between Mr. Stankovic and other departments and instances of this Tribunal. I think his position is clear. What he wants to say is that -- or rather, I don't think he has any intention of violating the rules, but wanted to respect them. And it is in that respect that I should like to receive confirmation from Mr. Stankovic that I understood him properly, that indeed that is what he wanted to do. That he, like all of us here, is vigilant and respects all the measures that have been taken by the Tribunal, put in place in these proceedings, protecting information, whatever that information may be. So I personally didn't gain the impression that Mr. Stankovic actually wanted to say anything other than that. And that is the point I would like you to give me assurances on, to tell me yes or no. Have I understood you correctly? Did I understand your line of thinking properly, that it was not your intention at any point?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. El Mahdi, you have understood things very well. May I just be allowed to expound this in greater detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please, Mr. Stankovic. I understood that you wanted to go into details. If you go into details, then we'll have to go into private session. I think that would be prudent. So Madam Registrar, may we go into private session for this portion of the proceedings, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: at 3.15 p.m.
